newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopian bank opens forex bureaux in Addis Ababa.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopian bank opens forex bureaux in Addis Ababa.

text.p: The state-owned Commercial Bank of Ethiopia (CBE) announced on Monday that it had opened the first forex bureaux in two of its branches in Addis Ababa's main commercial district.
The bank invited its clients in an advertisement published in local papers on Monday to visit the branches to meet their foreign currency requirements.
Kinfemichael Woldetinsae, general manager of exchange control at the central National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE), told Reuters commercial banks were allowed to open such bureaux in October last year.
He said the steps were taken as part of liberalisation in the financial sector started in 1992.
Kinfemichael said since the devaluation of the birr in 1992, restrictions in the forex market were gradually relaxed and in 1993 a forex auction was introduced to meet demand for imports.
"The introduction of forex bureaux would help to remove bureaucratic hurdles... people faced in their quest to get foreign currency," he said.
Three private banks with a total paid up capital of $75 million and other state-owned commercial banks were also expected to open up forex bureaux, he added.
A Commercial Bank of Ethiopia (CBE) official said frequent customers could draw up to $10,000 in foreign currency from the forex bureaus.
